# Run book: Schedule a message

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/schedule-a-message.md) | [Spec](../specs/schedule-a-message.md)

## Contents

- [Purpose](#purpose)

- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Purpose

Show a due-time event store with a hosted runner: items are leased so two instances never run the same one, and registering the same key again moves the due time.

## Preconditions

- The API runs with its hosted services on (not DISABLE_HOSTING=true).
- The signed-in user holds the schedule.use right (the admin role).

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "Schedule a message"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/messaging/schedule`:

1. **Schedule it.** Give the item a key, a delay and a message, then press Schedule. Expect: The item is listed under Pending with its due time. Earlier items that already ran are listed under Fired.
2. **Take it back.** Remove drops a pending item before it is due, so it never fires. Expect: The Pending list is empty again.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The item never moves to Fired | The API runs with DISABLE_HOSTING=true, so no runner polls the store | Start the API without that variable |
| Item refused | The key is empty or the delay is outside 0 to 3600 seconds | Enter a key and a delay in range |

Related framework features: OoBDev.ComplexEvents (`IScheduleStore`, `ScheduleRunner`); OoBDev.ComplexEvents.Hosting (`ScheduleHost`).
